mso-ascii-font-family: Calibri; mso-ascii-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-char-type: symbol; mso-hansi-font-family: Calibri; mso-hansi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-symbol-font-family: Wingdings;\"\u003Eà\u003C\/span\u003E\nclaiming moniker at various fields (also bagged 2 bronze medals in table tennis\nat PULSE-2013) and thus the college sports’ coordinator. A gourmand and a\nsight-seer, inter alia; and writing here to share the experiences of my primal\nbailiwick-MEDICAL SCIENCE!\u003C\/div\u003E\n\u003Cdiv class=\"MsoNormal\"\u003E\n\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\n\u003Cdiv class=\"MsoNormal\"\u003E\nI am in my 2\u003Csup\u003End\u003C\/sup\u003E proff in Chirayu Medical College\nand Hospital, Bhopal. Presently I am working under the guidance of Dr. Rakesh\nBiswas with the object of drafting a case report for the British medical\njournal. And this writing here presents my experience from the same… \u003C\/div\u003E\n\u003Cdiv class=\"MsoNormal\"\u003E\n\u003Cspan style=\"color: #222222; font-family: \u0026quot;Arial\u0026quot;,\u0026quot;sans-serif\u0026quot;; font-size: 10.0pt; line-height: 115%; mso-fareast-font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;;\"\u003EAs\nit is a tendency of humans to assume what’s going to happen before setting foot\non an unwearied path; I, in my heart, carried less doubt about the workshop I was\ngoing to attend. As especially in the domain of medical sciences, at\nmetaphorically a young age, we doctors are sure to expect sessions of\nbrainstorming and an unrelenting test of knowledge. But guess I was totally\nwrong this time!\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\n\u003Cdiv class=\"MsoNormal\" style=\"background-color: white; background-position: initial initial; background-repeat: initial initial; margin-bottom: 0.0001pt;\"\u003E\n\u003Cspan style=\"color: #222222; font-family: \u0026quot;Arial\u0026quot;,\u0026quot;sans-serif\u0026quot;; font-size: 10.0pt; mso-fareast-font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;;\"\u003EThough the entire\ncourse was a bit lethargic considering it required a 7 hours run in order to\ncover 40 odd kms, changing 4 public transports each day and working like this\nfor 14 consecutive days ; I am thankful it proved to be worth the effort!\u003Co:p\u003E\u003C\/o:p\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\n\u003Cdiv class=\"MsoNormal\" style=\"background-color: white; background-position: initial initial; background-repeat: initial initial; margin-bottom: 0.0001pt;\"\u003E\n\u003Cspan style=\"color: #222222; font-family: \u0026quot;Arial\u0026quot;,\u0026quot;sans-serif\u0026quot;; font-size: 10.0pt; mso-fareast-font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;;\"\u003EI reached People’s\nCollege of Medical Sciences on 19\u003Csup\u003Eth\u003C\/sup\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"color: #222222; font-family: \u0026quot;Arial\u0026quot;,\u0026quot;sans-serif\u0026quot;; font-size: 10.0pt; mso-bidi-font-size: 11.0pt; mso-fareast-font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"color: #222222; font-family: \u0026quot;Arial\u0026quot;,\u0026quot;sans-serif\u0026quot;; font-size: 10.0pt; mso-fareast-font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;;\"\u003EOctober at 9:00 am. Dr. Biswas was on his routine round when I\nfirst met him. It was in the casualty ward that I was introduced to him by\nSumit, a friend of mine who took up the course with me. And then the training\nbegan.\u003Co:p\u003E\u003C\/o:p\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\n\u003Cdiv class=\"MsoNormal\" style=\"background-color: white; background-position: initial initial; background-repeat: initial initial; margin-bottom: 0.0001pt;\"\u003E\n\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\n\u003Cdiv class=\"MsoNormal\" style=\"background-color: white; background-position: initial initial; background-repeat: initial initial; margin-bottom: 0.0001pt;\"\u003E\n\u003Cspan style=\"color: #222222; font-family: \u0026quot;Arial\u0026quot;,\u0026quot;sans-serif\u0026quot;; font-size: 10.0pt; mso-fareast-font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;;\"\u003ECase discussions-\u003Co:p\u003E\u003C\/o:p\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\n\u003Cdiv class=\"MsoNormal\" style=\"background-color: white; background-position: initial initial; background-repeat: initial initial; margin-bottom: 0.0001pt;\"\u003E\n\u003Cspan style=\"color: #222222; font-family: \u0026quot;Arial\u0026quot;,\u0026quot;sans-serif\u0026quot;; font-size: 10.0pt; mso-fareast-font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;;\"\u003EAs I stated earlier, I\nwas expecting loads and loads of lectures along with Power point presentations\nand a wall of tough questions to be put up by the doctor in-charge but it\nseemed I had a lot of air to keep!!\u003Co:p\u003E\u003C\/o:p\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\n\u003Cdiv class=\"MsoNormal\" style=\"background-color: white; background-position: initial initial; background-repeat: initial initial; margin-bottom: 0.0001pt;\"\u003E\n\u003Cspan style=\"color: #222222; font-family: \u0026quot;Arial\u0026quot;,\u0026quot;sans-serif\u0026quot;; font-size: 10.0pt; mso-fareast-font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;;\"\u003EDr. Biswas had this\nunique thing about his teaching prophecy whereby he discussed each and every\nlittle point about the patient with us. This was yet another experience in\nitself as being a 2\u003Csup\u003End\u003C\/sup\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"color: #222222; font-family: \u0026quot;Arial\u0026quot;,\u0026quot;sans-serif\u0026quot;; font-size: 10.0pt; mso-bidi-font-size: 11.0pt; mso-fareast-font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"color: #222222; font-family: \u0026quot;Arial\u0026quot;,\u0026quot;sans-serif\u0026quot;; font-size: 10.0pt; mso-fareast-font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;;\"\u003EProff student it is not very often that we are exposed to such\nopen discussions.\u003Co:p\u003E\u003C\/o:p\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\n\u003Cdiv class=\"MsoNormal\" style=\"background-color: white; background-position: initial initial; background-repeat: initial initial; margin-bottom: 0.0001pt;\"\u003E\n\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\n\u003Cdiv class=\"MsoNormal\" style=\"background-color: white; background-position: initial initial; background-repeat: initial initial; margin-bottom: 0.0001pt;\"\u003E\n\u003Cspan style=\"color: #222222; font-family: \u0026quot;Arial\u0026quot;,\u0026quot;sans-serif\u0026quot;; font-size: 10.0pt; mso-fareast-font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;;\"\u003EMY 1\u003Csup\u003Est\u003C\/sup\u003E\nCASE:-\u003Co:p\u003E\u003C\/o:p\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\n\u003Cdiv class=\"MsoNormal\" style=\"background-color: white; background-position: initial initial; background-repeat: initial initial; margin-bottom: 0.0001pt;\"\u003E\n\u003Cspan style=\"color: #222222; font-family: \u0026quot;Arial\u0026quot;,\u0026quot;sans-serif\u0026quot;; font-size: 10.0pt; mso-fareast-font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;;\"\u003EIt was the case of\ndiabetes mellitus with nephropathy. Just by a general discussion with the\npatient Biswas sir showed us how to infer the malady that that man suffered. The\npatient had severe D.V.T in lower limbs. Sir made us palpate it and made sure\nthat if we ever palpate such a limb we should easily be able to diagnose D.V.T.\nThis was indeed something different from mugging up pathology and complications\nof D.V.T from Robbins.\u003Co:p\u003E\u003C\/o:p\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\n\u003Cdiv class=\"MsoNormal\" style=\"background-color: white; background-position: initial initial; background-repeat: initial initial; margin-bottom: 0.0001pt;\"\u003E\n\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\n\u003Cdiv class=\"MsoNormal\" style=\"background-color: white; background-position: initial initial; background-repeat: initial initial; margin-bottom: 0.0001pt;\"\u003E\n\u003Cspan style=\"color: #222222; font-family: \u0026quot;Arial\u0026quot;,\u0026quot;sans-serif\u0026quot;; font-size: 10.0pt; mso-fareast-font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;;\"\u003EEXAMINING THE NEXT\nBED:-\u003Co:p\u003E\u003C\/o:p\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\n\u003Cdiv class=\"MsoNormal\" style=\"background-color: white; background-position: initial initial; background-repeat: initial initial; margin-bottom: 0.0001pt;\"\u003E\n\u003Cspan style=\"color: #222222; font-family: \u0026quot;Arial\u0026quot;,\u0026quot;sans-serif\u0026quot;; font-size: 10.0pt; mso-fareast-font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;;\"\u003EWe then moved to the\nnext bed where an 18 year old boy (did not seem to be 18 appeared to be 13 or\n14 years old) looked seriously ill. He was pale and malnourished. Dr. Biswas\ntold us that he also had hepatic failure and was very critical. That boy later died\nof Wilson’s disease, a rare copper storage disease. Through this case I learned\nmany things as it was a serious challenge to make exact diagnosis of his\ndisease, even for a team of highly qualified doctors. Since in Wilson’s disease\nlenticular degeneration also occurs I gave a suggestion to check the boys basic\nIQ. Dr. Biswas drew different shapes on his file and asked the boy to copy it.\nHe not only copied the shapes correctly but also made all the shapes of almost\nthe same size as drawn by Sir, which was a good result. This was definitely something\nnew I tried my hand on.\u003Co:p\u003E\u003C\/o:p\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\n\u003Cdiv class=\"MsoNormal\" style=\"background-color: white; background-position: initial initial; background-repeat: initial initial; margin-bottom: 0.0001pt;\"\u003E\n\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\n\u003Cdiv class=\"MsoNormal\" style=\"background-color: white; background-position: initial initial; background-repeat: initial initial; margin-bottom: 0.0001pt;\"\u003E\n\u003Cspan style=\"color: #222222; font-family: \u0026quot;Arial\u0026quot;,\u0026quot;sans-serif\u0026quot;; font-size: 10.0pt; mso-fareast-font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;;\"\u003EA ROUND AROUND THE\nOPD:-\u003Co:p\u003E\u003C\/o:p\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\n\u003Cdiv class=\"MsoNormal\" style=\"background-color: white; background-position: initial initial; background-repeat: initial initial; margin-bottom: 0.0001pt;\"\u003E\n\u003Cspan style=\"color: #222222; font-family: \u0026quot;Arial\u0026quot;,\u0026quot;sans-serif\u0026quot;; font-size: 10.0pt; mso-fareast-font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;;\"\u003EAfter taking up the\nindoor patients, the round in the OPD began.\u003Co:p\u003E\u003C\/o:p\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\n\u003Cdiv class=\"MsoNormal\" style=\"background-color: white; background-position: initial initial; background-repeat: initial initial; margin-bottom: 0.0001pt;\"\u003E\n\u003Cspan style=\"color: #222222; font-family: \u0026quot;Arial\u0026quot;,\u0026quot;sans-serif\u0026quot;; font-size: 10.0pt; mso-fareast-font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;;\"\u003EDuring this sir told\nus about a website called\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"color: #222222; font-family: \u0026quot;Arial\u0026quot;,\u0026quot;sans-serif\u0026quot;; font-size: 10.0pt; mso-bidi-font-size: 11.0pt; mso-fareast-font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"color: #222222; font-family: \u0026quot;Arial\u0026quot;,\u0026quot;sans-serif\u0026quot;; font-size: 10.0pt; mso-fareast-font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;;\"\u003E\u003Ca href=\"http:\/\/udhc.co.in\/\" target=\"_blank\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"color: #1155cc; mso-bidi-font-size: 11.0pt;\"\u003EUDHC.CO.IN\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/a\u003E, how it was made and how it benefits not\nonly the middle class but also the poor people. UDHC is basically a user driven\nhealth care website through which a patient can be followed easily without\nrevealing his\/her identity just by giving him\/her a botanical name. All you\nneed to do is to enter the history in the INPUT tab with the consent signed by\nthe patient and share it. It is also a very helpful tool in taking a piece of\nadvice or sharing a case with fellow doctors around the world. I personally found\nit to be a unique and an innovative step which has helped the sufferers to\nconsult reputed doctors around the world now for free. But for us it undeniably\nbecame a platform to discuss our findings with experienced doctors.\u003Co:p\u003E\u003C\/o:p\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\n\u003Cdiv class=\"MsoNormal\" style=\"background-color: white; background-position: initial initial; background-repeat: initial initial; margin-bottom: 0.0001pt;\"\u003E\n\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\n\u003Cdiv class=\"MsoNormal\" style=\"background-color: white; background-position: initial initial; background-repeat: initial initial; margin-bottom: 0.0001pt;\"\u003E\n\u003Cspan style=\"color: #222222; font-family: \u0026quot;Arial\u0026quot;,\u0026quot;sans-serif\u0026quot;; font-size: 10.0pt; mso-fareast-font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;;\"\u003EIn the OPD we came\nacross a patient who was a 31 years old man with a complaint of vomiting,\nnausea and a non-radiating pain in the right upper abdomen from past 30 days.\nDuring those 30 days he had an apparent loss of weight with marked anorexia.\nThere was a decrease in his bowel movement and an increase in flatulence.\u003Cbr \/\u003E\nThe patient had no difficulty in swallowing and the vomit contained\nrecognizable food particles eaten several hours back. Neither black stools nor\nrectal bleeding was observed. He told us that he used to be\u003Co:p\u003E\u003C\/o:p\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\n\u003Cdiv class=\"MsoNormal\" style=\"background-color: white; background-position: initial initial; background-repeat: initial initial; margin-bottom: 0.0001pt;\"\u003E\n\u003Cspan style=\"color: #222222; font-family: \u0026quot;Arial\u0026quot;,\u0026quot;sans-serif\u0026quot;; font-size: 10.0pt; mso-fareast-font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;;\"\u003Ea non-vegetarian and used\nto consume 250 gm of meat thrice a week previously but has had been a pure vegetarian\nfor the last 6 years. He also consumed tobacco (gutka) 8-10 packs daily and alcohol\n(180ml) once or twice a week.\u003Cbr \/\u003E\nHe had neither a past history nor a family history of such a problem.\u003Cbr \/\u003E\nEndoscopy showed: deformed, shortened bulb with inability to push scope into\n2nd part of duodenum.\u003Cbr \/\u003E\nBlood report:-Mild anemia.\u003Cbr \/\u003E\nR.B.C showed: mild anisopoikilocytosis with microcytes.\u003Cbr \/\u003E\nW.B.C showed: normal total count \u0026amp; normal.\u003Co:p\u003E\u003C\/o:p\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\n\u003Cdiv class=\"MsoNormal\" style=\"background-color: white; background-position: initial initial; background-repeat: initial initial; margin-bottom: 0.0001pt;\"\u003E\n\u003Cspan style=\"color: #222222; font-family: \u0026quot;Arial\u0026quot;,\u0026quot;sans-serif\u0026quot;; font-size: 10.0pt; mso-fareast-font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;;\"\u003EFrom his complaints of\nthe last 30 days and considering the endoscopy report findings I proposed that the\npossibility of duodenal ulcer was pretty less. According to me it was a case of\nobstruction due to polyps of GI tract. Biswas sir and I discussed for a while\nand he was then extended a treatment for ulcers. But due to a difference of\nopinion we have asked him to visit us over the next fortnight to track the\nsuccess of the treatment.\u003Co:p\u003E\u003C\/o:p\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\n\u003Cdiv class=\"MsoNormal\" style=\"background-color: white; background-position: initial initial; background-repeat: initial initial; margin-bottom: 0.0001pt;\"\u003E\n\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\n\u003Cdiv class=\"MsoNormal\" style=\"background-color: white; background-position: initial initial; background-repeat: initial initial; margin-bottom: 0.0001pt;\"\u003E\n\u003Cspan style=\"color: #222222; font-family: \u0026quot;Arial\u0026quot;,\u0026quot;sans-serif\u0026quot;; font-size: 10.0pt; mso-fareast-font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;;\"\u003EOne-on-one interaction\nwith the patients has been one of the major benefits of this program. Sir gave\nus complete freedom to examine the patient up till our will and to spend as\nmuch time as required to extract all the information in order to solve the\npatient’s problem. It was as if we were the pilot of the Boeing loaded with the\npassengers, with total authority and in charge!\u003Co:p\u003E\u003C\/o:p\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\n\u003Cdiv class=\"MsoNormal\" style=\"background-color: white; background-position: initial initial; background-repeat: initial initial; margin-bottom: 0.0001pt;\"\u003E\n\u003Cspan style=\"color: #222222; font-family: \u0026quot;Arial\u0026quot;,\u0026quot;sans-serif\u0026quot;; font-size: 10.0pt; mso-fareast-font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;;\"\u003ESir also gave us the\npermission to utilize the research lab in which we could perform basic yet very\nimportant hematological and biochemical tests. Through this we realized how\neven a small lab with minimal resources can be used to make powerful diagnoses.\u003Co:p\u003E\u003C\/o:p\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\n\u003Cdiv class=\"MsoNormal\" style=\"background-color: white;
